Forwarding Samir's thread — Arctic Supplies hitting 'session fingerprint mismatch' on invite acceptance. They provided a header capture that looks like TLS offload + host/forwarded rewrites.

Why I'm escalating: if a proxy is rewriting headers or stripping Set-Cookie/Authorization bits we can get OTP validation failures because the server-side fingerprint (derived from headers + cookie) doesn't line up with the client's subsequent request. That can appear as 'fingerprint mismatch' even though OTP itself is valid.

Asks:
- Can infra confirm if our acceptance endpoint is tolerant of X-Forwarded-* changes?
- Any known cases where TLS termination or header rewrites cause fingerprint failures with Coupa-style invite flows?
- If this is infra, what short-term config change can we prescribe to Arctic (proxy rule or bypass) so they can accept supplier invites today?

I created a Jira: INF-8472 and marked it P1 for customer-facing onboarding block. Samir's procurement team needs the supplier live by Friday to attach a PO.

Thanks for the escalation — I dug into the header dump Samir provided and reproduced a similar flow in our staging environment. Quick summary:

Findings:
- Arctic's header dump shows their proxy rewriting the Host and adding an X-Edge-Token header; more importantly the proxy is stripping the incoming Set-Cookie on the acceptance response in certain cases (see attached arctic-sre-headers.txt).
- Our session fingerprint uses a combination of cookie + minimal client fingerprint (User-Agent + originating IP / forwarded-for when available). If Set-Cookie doesn't arrive at the client, the client never presents the cookie back and the fingerprint check fails.

Short-term recommendation (customer-actionable):
1) Add a passthrough rule on the TLS offload for coupa.arcticsupplies.com so Set-Cookie and Set-Cookie-SameSite headers are preserved; or configure the proxy to not rewrite Host for paths under /supplier/accept. This will restore cookie flow immediately.
2) As a fallback, Arctic can accept invites from a non-proxied IP (off VPN) while they roll the proxy change.

Longer-term: infra to investigate making the acceptance flow tolerant of missing forwarded IPs when cookie-less; but that requires product changes (INF-8472).

I've attached a small script we used in staging to show the cookie exchange (arctic-sre-headers.txt). I'll post an internal runbook for support to follow when customers report similar failures.

ETA: If Arctic applies the passthrough rule we expect acceptance to work within minutes; we can validate with them and close the ticket.

-Ben
